paper_id: Boudreaux et al., The Case for AI Loss of Control Response Planning and an Outline to Get Started, RAND PE-A4232-1, October 2025

passages_found.quote: As artificial intelligence (AI) systems become increasingly capable and diffused throughout the economy and society, the possibility of loss of control (LOC) incidents in which AI systems operate outside human control may require new national-level responses. In this paper, the authors describe the case for a national plan to respond to LOC incidents and propose key criteria and an outline to get started.

As artificial intelligence (AI) systems become increasingly capable and diffused throughout the economy and society, the possibility of loss of control (LOC) incidents—in which AI systems operate outside meaningful human control—may require new national response capabilities, preparedness, and planning.

passages_found.quote: Experiments in controlled conditions increasingly find that advanced AI models demonstrate behavior that could evade human control, including deceiving or blackmailing users to prevent themselves from being replaced or shut down. Although these real-world incidents and experimental findings may be detected and quickly remediated, there is potential for LOC incidents to escalate to greater levels of harm, particularly if they occur in high-stakes domains or if human oversight is too slow or insufficient before serious consequences unfold.
passages_found.location: The Case for AI Loss of Control Response Planning and an Outline to Get Started, p. 1

passages_found.quote: We define LOC incidents as incidents in which AI systems operate outside meaningful human control.

We define rogue AI as an AI system that is responsible for LOC incidents regardless of whether the LOC was accidental or resulted from external manipulation. In other words, our definition encompasses scenarios in which humans have inadvertently deployed an AI system without adequate control mechanisms, humans deliberately create or deploy rogue AI systems for malicious purposes, and advanced AI systems themselves develop capabilities that enable them to evade human control.

Our definition can be compared with the definition of LOC scenario from the 2025 United Kingdom (UK) AI Safety Report, which reads: 'Loss of control scenario: A scenario in which one or more general-purpose AI systems come to operate outside of anyone's control, with no clear path to regaining control' (AI Safety Institute, International AI Safety Report 2025, Department for Science, Innovation and Technology, UK Government, February 18, 2025) (emphasis added).
